# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- The full checks and tests run on GitHub, in the kit's CI run, not on your machine: a task is
  done only when HEAD has a passing CI run and is on `origin/main`. Use Kition's
  `scripts/kit-ci.sh` (`push`, `wait`, `failures`, `land`; Kition's `docs/kits.md`, section
  4c). Compile only the crates you touched locally.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gating test.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Work on `kition-slide` only in its main checkout; never change, build, or commit in its worktrees (`kition-slide-wt/*`, `kition-*-wt`, `kition-naming-work`).
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.photo` kit. These rules come first; the guide below still
applies to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/sdk/editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with Kition Photo's menu bar, options bar, toolbox, canvas tools, and
  Properties and Layers panels; a host (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows it in an
  iframe and talks to it over the Kit UI protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, kition-sdk `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only with the host's theme tokens and kit-editor components;
  menu labels and command titles are Kition Photo's English text, translated by its
  `web/src/i18n/upstream/*.tsv` catalogs, and the editor's own strings live in
  `web/src/strings.ts` (`en-US`, `zh-CN`). Files go only through the host.
- The engine is compiled to WebAssembly by `bindings/wasm` and runs in a Web Worker. The contract (methods, `renderArea` box exactness, `save`
  without marking saved, `markSaved`) and the checklist for new kits are in Kition's
  `docs/kits.md`. The contract comes from the `KitionAI/kition-sdk` crate
  (`KitDocument`, `export_kit_document!`, `testing::check_contract`); `kition-photo-kit`
  implements it and must keep passing `check_contract`. Change the contract in kition-sdk,
  never here.
- `bindings/headless` runs headless for Kition's agent and must keep passing the Kit Protocol
  conformance suite (13 of 13). A clean document reloads when its file changed on disk; unsaved
  edits are never discarded.
- The whole repository is Apache-2.0 ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); third-party notices are listed in
  `NOTICE`. Upstream is credited only in NOTICE; never write upstream names anywhere else. Use the rustup stable
  toolchain (Rust 1.95 or newer). Build the SDK for Kition with `scripts/build-kit-module.sh photo`
  there.

# AGENTS.md: guide for AI agents and contributors

Kition Photo's engine is written in **Rust only** (no JavaScript or TypeScript); it is compiled to
WebAssembly for the kit's editor (`web/`, React on `@kition/sdk/editor`) and to a native binary for the
headless kit executable (`bindings/headless`). There is no native desktop UI and no browser build of
its own: Kition draws the editor in the page (see "Kition kit rules" above). The product name is
always written **Kition Photo** in user-facing text: UI, docs prose. Machine names stay lowercase:
crates (`kition-photo-*`), binaries, file names, ids (`ai.kition.photo`). The goal is close
Photoshop parity (same menus, shortcuts, behaviour and file fidelity) with good performance, and
every feature drivable by agents. Read this file first, then `docs/`.

## 1. Orientation (5 minutes)

| Read | Why |
|---|---|
| `docs/architecture.md` | Crate map, dependency layers, the engine/UI seam, document model |
| `docs/development.md` | Build, test, run, debug tricks, test corpora, rendering fidelity |
| `crates/<name>/README.md` (where present) | Public API of that crate |
| `docs/development.md` › Test corpora | Real-file test oracles: public psd-tools, ag-psd, PngSuite and other sets fetched into `corpus/` by `cargo xtask corpus --all` at the pins in `tools/xtask/src/corpus_pins.rs`; the Photoshop-authored PSDs are the maintainers' private corpus (not distributed) |

## 2. Workspace map

```text
crates/                        engine crates, grouped as crates/<group>/<name>
  support/  geom cms color                  L0 foundation (geometry, ICC colour management, pixel formats + blend math)
            text                            L2 type engine
  render/   raster                          L0 COW tiles
  formats/  psd codecs heif raw affinity    standalone format crates (no workspace deps; publishable)
            format io                       L3 .kphoto native format; L4 document <-> PSD / flat formats
  engine/   doc                             L1 document model (layers, masks, adjustments, effects, object layers: pure data)
            ops paint algo vector           L2 history, brush engine, imaging algorithms, paths/shapes
            compose                         L3 CPU compositor (the oracle)
            plugins                         L4 sandboxed WebAssembly plug-ins
            engine                          L5 Session + command registry (every action is a command)
            automation                      L6 automation server used by the headless kit
  kdm/      kdm-model                       L5 KDM replica bridge
bindings/
  wasm      kition-photo-kit                the engine behind Kition's KitDocument contract, compiled to WebAssembly
  headless  kition-photo                    the headless kit executable for Kition's agent (Kit Protocol)
web/                           the kit's editor (React, on @kition/sdk/editor)
examples/plugins/invert-rs     an example WebAssembly filter plug-in (not a workspace member)
tools/
  xtask/                       cargo xtask layers | wasm | ci | stats | corpus | test-corpus | version | eval
  scripts/                     fetch-corpus.sh, layered_tiff_fixtures.py
```

**Layering is enforced** by `cargo xtask layers`. A crate may depend only on lower layers. `psd`, `codecs` and `cms` depend on nothing in the workspace. A new crate must be registered in `tools/xtask/src/layers.rs`.

## 3. Core rules

### Never crash (outranks feature work)

People trust Kition Photo with their work, and a crash loses it. A malformed file, a bad command param, a corrupt settings file, an odd keystroke or a full disk must produce an error the user or agent can act on, never a panic. Don't ship a feature by adding a panic path; fix a crash before building on top of it.

- **Non-test code never panics.** No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or `unimplemented!`. Return the crate's error type and propagate with `?`; use `ok_or(..)?`, `let .. else { return Err(..) }`, `if let`, or `unwrap_or*` where a fallback is truly correct (never one that silently corrupts a document). Unfinished features return an "unsupported" error. The only exception is a provably infallible literal: `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` plus `.expect("why it can't fail")`.
- **No `unsafe`.** The workspace sets `unsafe_code = "forbid"` with no exceptions. Don't add `unsafe` anywhere.
- **Input-derived numbers are hostile.** Use `get()` rather than `[i]`/`[a..b]` for indices from files, params, selections or arithmetic on them; slice strings only at char boundaries; use `checked_*`/`saturating_*` for lengths, offsets and counts; guard division by zero and NaN/inf casts; cap allocations sized by input.
- **Bound recursion** with depth limits or seen-sets (documents can be deep or cyclic).
- **Don't cascade.** Handle lock poisoning (`lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)`) and treat thread joins as `Result`s.
- **Last-resort guard.** The kit executable must catch an escaped panic around command dispatch and file import/export, report it as an error and keep the document. It's a safety net, not a licence to panic.
- **Prove it.** Every crash fix comes with a small synthetic regression test that panicked before the fix.
- **Enforced by clippy.** `.clippy.toml` allows `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`/indexing in tests only. Clean crates carry `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`; new crates start with it.

1. **Everything is a command.** New user-visible behaviour = a command in the engine (`crates/engine/engine/src/*_cmds.rs`, registered in `commands.rs`) with id, label, menu path, shortcut, params doc, `enabled` and `run`, plus tests. The editor, the headless kit executable and its automation all dispatch commands by id.
2. **No format or colour assumptions.** Bit depth (8/16/32f) and colour model (RGB/Gray/CMYK/Lab…) are runtime data. Never introduce a `u8`-only pixel path in public APIs. Never assume sRGB: colour conversions go through `kition-photo-cms` (`Transform`, `transform::cached`). Test at several depths.
3. **Clean-room.** We studied Photoshop and other proprietary editors for *behaviour and look only*. Never copy their code, shaders, profiles or assets. Implement from public specs (Adobe PSD spec, ICC, ISO 32000 blend modes, papers) and observation. Third-party assets must be permissively licensed, keep their license file next to them, and get a row in `docs/attribution.md` (path, title, author, source, license) in the same change; so do original assets. **Never commit font files:** fonts live in [KitionAI/kition-fonts](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-fonts). Kition Photo uses it through the optional build input `KITION_FONTS_DIR=<kition-fonts checkout>` (read by `crates/support/text/build.rs`, exposed as `kition_photo_text::KITION_FONTS`; empty without it, and everything must still work). Build with it: `KITION_FONTS_DIR="$PWD/../kition-fonts" cargo build`; details in `docs/development.md` › Fonts.
4. **Tests are the gate.** Every change comes with tests. Format crates use round-trip, synthetic-generator, oracle and fuzz tests. Keep the PSD corpus results from regressing.
5. **The editor is thin and data-driven.** `web/` holds only view/window state; all document edits go through the engine's commands, by id, the same way the headless kit executable and the agent do.
6. **Never break wasm.** L0–L5 (plus `kition-photo-kit`) must `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (run `cargo xtask wasm`). File-system code is `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))` or goes through the platform services.
7. **Performance is a feature.** Benchmark heavy operations on a 24–36 MP image in release. Work per tile in parallel (rayon), skip empty tiles, never scan a full surface per frame (cache per revision), and record before/after timings in the dev log.

8. **Never panic on input** (see *Never crash* above). A command's `run` closure and anything it calls must return `Err`, never panic, for *any* params or document state: validate params, check bounds before indexing or dividing, and reject absurd sizes before allocating. The `panic_hunt` integration test fuzzes every command with adversarial params and must stay green.

## 4. Before you finish a task

On this machine run only the fast checks:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check -p <crates you touched> --all-targets
cargo xtask wasm            # if you touched L0–L5 or kition-photo-kit
cd web && pnpm typecheck    # if you touched web/
```

The full checks run in the kit's CI run on GitHub (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which calls
Kition's reusable kit CI): clippy, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask ci` (fmt + clippy +
tests + layers + wasm) and every `test:*` script of `web/`. A task is done when the CI run of
HEAD passes and HEAD is on `origin/main` (Kition's `scripts/kit-ci.sh` `push`, `wait`, `land`).
Add no other workflows, and do not start the Package workflow (`.github/workflows/package.yml`):
releasing is the owner's step.

Two checks are not part of the CI run; run them yourself when they apply:

```sh
cargo test -p kition-photo-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored   # if you added/changed commands: no panic on adversarial input (Rule 8)
cargo xtask test-corpus     # if you touched psd, io, codecs, compose, text or format (or: --changed decides)
```

**Test corpora.** Real-file corpora live in `corpus/` (gitignored, never committed), fetched at pinned commits and sha256-verified by `cargo xtask corpus --all`: psd-tools, ag-psd, PngSuite and the other public sets from their upstreams. The Photoshop-authored oracles (`corpus/photoshop`) are maintained privately by the maintainers and not distributed: `--all` skips them, maintainers copy them from their clone with `--local`, and their tests are skipped without them. Pins: `tools/xtask/src/corpus_pins.rs`. The corpus tests are opt-in (cargo feature `corpus`): plain `cargo test` skips them, and with the feature on a missing public corpus fails ("run `cargo xtask corpus --all`"). `cargo xtask test-corpus` fetches and runs them all. Never commit corpus files.

Commands must **never panic** on bad input (Rule 8): every `run` closure and the code it calls returns `Err`, not a panic, for any params or document state. New commands come with a graceful-failure test (empty/out-of-range/wrong-type params → `Err`, not a crash).

Then append a terse entry to `log/devlog.md` (what landed, numbers, what's still open) if you keep one. Keep the tree building at every step.

## 5. Parallel agents

- Use your own target dir (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/agent-<name>`) to avoid the Cargo build lock, and edit only the files you own. Shared files (`engine/src/lib.rs`, the `v.extend(...)` list in `engine/src/commands.rs`) get small, surgical edits; re-read before editing.
- Put new commands in a **new module** (`engine/src/<area>_cmds.rs` with a `specs()` function) rather than growing a shared file.
- If someone else's in-progress edit breaks the build, wait and retry; don't fix their files.
- Keep every `Cargo.toml` valid at all times: the `crates/*` glob means one broken manifest breaks everyone's build. **Create or rewrite manifests atomically**: write to a temp file outside `crates/`, then `mv` it into place.
- Disk space: each target dir is about 10 GB. Delete `target/agent-*` dirs of finished agents.

## 6. Keeping the native format complete

`kition-photo-format` deliberately fails to compile when a `kition-photo-doc` struct gains a field, so
nothing is silently dropped from `.kphoto` saves. When you add a doc field, add it to
`crates/formats/format/src/manifest.rs` and `convert.rs` with `#[serde(default)]` so older files still load.
If the field has a PSD equivalent, map it in `crates/formats/io` too, and keep unknown PSD blocks verbatim.
